en: And Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh narrated it to us from al-Layth ibn Sa'd (H). And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: al-Thaqafi informed us: Ayyub narrated to us (H). And Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from my grandfather, from Ayyub (H). And Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah ibn Zayd informed me (H). And Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Abu Salamah al-Khuza'i narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Akhi al-Majishun informed us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar; all of them from Nafi', from al-Qasim, from Aisha, with this hadith, and some of them had a more complete narration of it than others. And in the hadith of Ibn Akhi al-Majishun, he added: She said: "So I took it and made it into two cushions, and he would recline upon them in the house."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha, that she bought a cushion with pictures on it. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw it, he stood at the door and did not enter. I recognized, or displeasure was recognized on his face. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I repent to Allah and to His Messenger; what sin have I committed?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "What is the matter with this cushion?" She said: "I bought it for you to sit upon and recline upon." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the makers of these images will be punished, and it will be said to them: Bring to life that which you created." Then he said: "Indeed, the house in which there are images is not entered by angels."

And Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us that Bukayr narrated to him that Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to him that his father narrated to him, from Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that she hung a curtain with pictures on it, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered and pulled it down. She said: "So I cut it into two pillows." A man in the gathering then, named Rabi'ah ibn Ata', the freed slave of Banu Zuhrah, said: "Did you not hear Abu Muhammad mention that Aisha said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would recline upon them?" Ibn al-Qasim said: "No." He said: "But I have heard him," meaning al-Qasim ibn Muhammad.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered upon me while I had hung a patterned curtain that had pictures on it, so he removed it, and I made two pillows out of it.

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated it to us from Sa'id ibn Amir (H). And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Abu Amir al-Aqadi informed us; all of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, he said: I heard al-Qasim narrating from Aisha that she had a garment containing pictures spread across an alcove, and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was praying facing it. He said: "Remove it from my sight." She said: "So I removed it and made it into cushions."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to us from Ibn Uyaynah—and the wording is Zuhayr's: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, that he heard Aisha saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered upon me while I had screened an alcove of mine with a curtain containing images. When he saw it, he tore it down, his face changed color, and he said: "O Aisha, the people most severely punished by Allah on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate the creation of Allah." Aisha said: "So we cut it up and made a pillow or two pillows from it."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Zuhayr ibn Harb all narrated it to us from Ibn Uyaynah (H). And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, they said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of narration. And in their hadith: "Indeed, the people most severely punished..." They did not mention 'among' (min).

And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, that Aisha narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered upon her; the like of the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, except that he said: "Then he reached toward the curtain and tore it down with his hand."

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered upon me while I had screened myself with a curtain containing an image. His face changed color, then he took hold of the curtain and tore it down, then said: "Indeed, among the people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who emulate the creation of Allah."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abdah narrated to us (H). And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Waki' narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and in the hadith of Abdah there is no mention of 'he returned from a journey.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) returned from a journey while I had screened my door with a patterned curtain that had winged horses on it. He ordered me, so I took it down.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Dawud, from Azrah, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'd ibn Hisham, from Aisha, who said: We had a curtain with the figure of a bird on it, and whenever anyone entered, it would face him. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "Move this away, for whenever I enter and see it, I remember this world." She said: And we had a velvet cloth whose border we used to say was silk, and we used to wear it. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to me: Ibn Abi Adi and Abd al-A'la narrated to us, with this chain of narration; Ibn al-Muthanna said: And he added in it—meaning Abd al-A'la—"And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not command us to cut it."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from Sa'id ibn Yasar Abu al-Hubab, the freed slave of Banu al-Najjar, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, from Abu Talhah al-Ansari, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or statues." He said: So I came to Aisha and said: "This person informs me that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or statues. Did you hear the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) mention that?" She said: "No, but I will tell you what I saw him do. I saw him go out for his military campaign, so I took a patterned cloth and hung it over the door. When he returned and saw the patterned cloth, I recognized displeasure on his face, so he pulled it until he tore it down or cut it, and said: Indeed, Allah did not command us to clothe stones and clay. She said: So we cut two cushions from it and I stuffed them with palm fiber, and he did not find fault with me for that."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj narrated to him that Busr ibn Sa'id narrated to him that Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani narrated to him—and Ubayd Allah al-Khawlani was with Busr—that Abu Talhah narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The angels do not enter a house in which there is an image." Busr said: Then Zayd ibn Khalid fell ill, so we visited him, and behold, in his house was a curtain with pictures on it. I said to Ubayd Allah al-Khawlani: "Did he not narrate to us concerning pictures?" He said: "Indeed, he said: except a pattern on a garment. Did you not hear him?" I said: "No." He said: "Yes, he certainly mentioned that."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Bukayr, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Zayd ibn Khalid, from Abu Talhah, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the angels do not enter a house in which there is an image." Busr said: Later, Zayd fell ill, so we visited him, and behold, on his door was a curtain with an image on it. He said: I said to Ubayd Allah al-Khawlani, the stepson of Maymunah the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Did not Zayd inform us about images the first day?" Ubayd Allah said: "Did you not hear him when he said: except a pattern on a garment?"

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, they said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, the like of the hadith of Yunus and his mention of the narrations in the chain.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah, that he heard Ibn Abbas say: I heard Abu Talhah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Yahya and Ishaq said: informed us, and the other two said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, from Abu Talhah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Sabbaq, that Abd Allah ibn Abbas said: Maymunah informed me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) woke up one morning silent and sullen. Maymunah said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have noticed a change in your disposition today." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Gabriel had promised to meet me last night, but he did not meet me. By Allah, he never broke a promise to me." He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remained in that state for the rest of that day. Then it occurred to him that there was a puppy under a tent of ours. He ordered it to be taken out, and it was taken out. Then he took water in his hand and sprinkled its place. When evening came, Gabriel met him, and he said to him: "You had promised to meet me last night." He said: "Yes, but we do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image." That morning, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered the killing of dogs, to the extent that he would order the killing of the dog of a small orchard and spare the dog of a large orchard.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: al-Makhzumi informed us: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, with this chain of narration, that Gabriel promised the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to come to him; and he mentioned the hadith and did not lengthen it as Ibn Abi Hazim had lengthened it.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, that she said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) promised the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to come to him at a certain hour. That hour arrived, but he did not come. In the Prophet's hand was a staff, so he threw it from his hand and said: "Neither Allah nor His messengers break their promise." Then he turned and behold, there was a puppy under his bed. He said: "O Aisha, when did this dog enter here?" She said: "By Allah, I did not know." So he ordered it to be taken out, and it was taken out. Then Gabriel came, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "You made an appointment with me and I sat waiting for you, but you did not come." He said: "The dog that was in your house prevented me; indeed, we do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya's; Yahya said: informed us, and the others said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah and Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the Jews and the Christians do not dye their hair, so differ from them."

And Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: Abu Quhafah was brought on the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, with his head and beard white like the thaghamah plant. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Change this with something, and avoid black."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: Abu Quhafah was brought, or he came in the year of the Conquest, or on the Day of the Conquest, with his head and beard like the thagham or thaghamah plant. He ordered, or he was ordered to be taken to his womenfolk, and he said: "Change this with something."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ibn Numayr, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Ismail—namely Ibn Ulayyah—narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that a man should perfume himself with saffron.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu al-Rabi', and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us; Yahya said: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, and the other two said: Hammad narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade perfuming oneself with saffron. Qutaybah said: Hammad said: meaning for men.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Numayr, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim all narrated to us from Ibn Uyaynah (H). And Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me, they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me (H). And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, they said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; all of them from al-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle, that he saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) lying on his back in the mosque, placing one of his legs over the other.

And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us: Ubayd Allah—meaning Ibn al-Akhnas—narrated to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should lie on his back and then place one of his legs over the other."
